claims.text: Rapidly quenched nominal FeCoNiTi has a dual-phase microstructure consisting of an fcc matrix and hexagonal C14 Laves precipitates.
The fcc matrix in the dual-phase FeCoNiTi alloy is ferromagnetic.
Changing Ti content modulates the volume fraction and morphology of the C14 Laves phase.
Thermal treatment at 400 K stabilizes the magnetic ground state.
The fcc/C14 interface exhibits lattice mismatch and Ti enrichment.
Lattice mismatch and Ti segregation at the fcc/C14 interface facilitate antiferromagnetic exchange interactions.
The Ti-rich C14 sublattice couples antiferromagnetically to the Fe/Co/Ni-rich fcc matrix.
Antiferromagnetic interphase coupling suppresses the effective magnetic moment and saturation magnetization of the fcc phase.
The C14 phase acts as a rigid magnetic-domain-wall pinning center because of its distinct crystal structure and magnetic anisotropy.
Domain-wall pinning and magnetic anisotropy associated with the C14 phase increase coercivity.
The dual-phase alloy will exhibit a coercivity of approximately 667 Oe at 400 K.
The dual-phase alloy will have lower saturation magnetization than its single-phase fcc counterpart.
Single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni has coercivity capped at 100 Oe because of insufficient orbital moments.
Single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni lacks effective magnetic pinning mechanisms.
Effective enhancement requires a continuous or semi-continuous C14 network.
Isolated, non-interacting C14 particles may fail to couple effectively to the fcc matrix.
Rapid quenching or reducing Ti below its solubility limit can produce a single-phase fcc FeCoNiTi control.
Spin-polarized first-principles density-of-states calculations at the Fermi level will be performed for the fcc matrix and C14 phase.
A C14-containing sample and a single-phase fcc control will be compared using 400 K hysteresis, torque magnetometry, and Barkhausen-noise measurements.
The hypothesis is falsified if the C14-containing sample remains below 200 Oe at 400 K, or if a single-phase fcc control substantially exceeds 100 Oe.

contradictions.description: The comparator is inconsistently defined as single-phase fcc FeCoNiTi without a Ti-induced Laves phase, Ti-free FeCoNi, and again single-phase fcc FeCoNiTi. These controls differ compositionally and cannot be treated as the same baseline.

The central mechanism asserts antiferromagnetic coupling to a Ti-rich or non-magnetic Ti sublattice, while the uncertainty field states that the C14 phase may instead be non-magnetic or possess unconfirmed antiferromagnetic order. The identity and magnetic character of the coupled moments are therefore internally unresolved.
